title: Which animals make the longest migrations?
examples: Which animal has the longest migration?
How do scientists track migrating animals?

explain.say: Some animals travel astonishing distances every year, following food, warmth and safe places to breed. The record holder is a seabird that weighs only about 100 grams.

draw.text: Which animals make the longest migrations?

explain.say: Arctic terns breed in the Arctic summer, then fly to the Antarctic for the southern summer, zigzagging to follow the winds. Tracking showed they fly about 70,000 kilometres a year; over a 30-year life, that is like flying to the Moon and back three times.
Grey and humpback whales swim between cold feeding waters near the poles and warm waters where they give birth, round trips that can reach 16,000 to 20,000 kilometres, often barely eating on the way.

Why go so far? Arctic terns enjoy two summers a year and see more daylight than any other animal, feeding in rich polar seas. Whales fatten up in food-rich cold water, then give birth in warm, calm seas where calves are safer.

faq.q: Which animal has the longest migration?
faq.a: The Arctic tern. Tracking with tiny devices showed these birds fly about 70,000 kilometres a year between the Arctic and the Antarctic, the longest regular migration known.
asks: How far does an Arctic tern fly?

faq.q: How do scientists track migrating animals?
faq.a: They fit animals with tags: tiny light sensors weighing about a gram for small birds, GPS and satellite tags for larger animals, and rings or photos of markings such as whale tail patterns.
asks: How do we know where animals migrate?

faq.q: Why do whales migrate to warm water to give birth?
faq.a: Newborn calves have little blubber, so warm water helps them stay warm, and calm tropical waters have fewer killer whales. The adults feed little there and live off fat stored in polar feeding grounds.
asks: Why do humpbacks go to the tropics?

faq.q: What is the longest nonstop flight by a bird?
faq.a: A bar-tailed godwit tracked in 2022 flew about 13,560 kilometres nonstop from Alaska to Tasmania in 11 days, without eating, drinking or landing.
asks: Can birds fly for days without stopping?
How far can a godwit fly?

faq.a: Yes. Monarch butterflies fly up to about 4,000 kilometres to Mexico, and globe skimmer dragonflies cross the Indian Ocean in a round trip spread over several generations.

facts: Tracked Arctic terns flew on average about 70,900 km a year (Egevang and colleagues, 2010).
A western grey whale named Varvara swam about 22,500 km on a round trip across the Pacific in 2011.
